rationale: The workflow already caches dependencies (Composer vendor, PHP extensions, npm) and sets a job timeout, so the dependency-cache and custom-timeout patterns are already satisfied; adding another dependency cache would hit the 'equivalent cache already exists' contraindication. The supported, not-yet-applied optimization that fits is P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: cancel superseded runs. This workflow triggers on push/pull_request to the workflow file, so repeated pushes to the same branch launch redundant Copilot setup runs and a newer revision supersedes the older one. Adding a per-ref concurrency group with cancel-in-progress stops the stale runner while the latest run completes the same setup, preserving every build/test step and coverage. No permissions are weakened, no secrets/publishing/deployment added, and no new network access introduced.
